newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Deputy head of Russia Duma - budget likely to pass.
newsitem.headline: Deputy head of Russia Duma - budget likely to pass.

text.p: The pro-government, first deputy speaker of the Russian Duma lower house of parliament said on Monday parliament would likely pass the 1997 budget soon.

"One of the reasons that the 1997 budget will be passed in the next few days is that the government has proposed a 'budget for growth' on the initiative of members of the State Duma," Alexander Shokhin told the Russian Chamber of Commerce.
Shokhin, a member of the pro-government Our Home Is Russia party, said the new budget leaned more towards active industrial policy by the government.

The budget, introduced by the government on Friday and which leaders of the Communist Party, the largest Duma bloc, said should be rejected, offered higher spending and higher income than earlier drafts.

It proposed the same deficit as earlier drafts, 3.5 percent of gross domestic product by Russia's calculations, and will be given a first reading by the Duma on Sunday, December 15, a working day in Russia.
Shokhin also called for the Duma to pass languishing amendments to a production-sharing law, which would strengthen the rights of foreign investors in natural resources, especially oil.
"The production-sharing law has been passed, but its full weight is not felt," he said, saying 10 amendments needed to pass.
"There are a number of examples, unfortunately, where we can see unpassed laws which would deliver a wide secure base of investors."
Shokhin criticised the government, represented at the meeting by Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin, for not coordinating macro-economic policy and restructuring policy.
Yasin said liberalisation of the economy had been a "concrete step forward' for Russia.
But he said Russian industry was still in decline and called for decreased privileges and handouts by the government.
